independent_primary_source_spot_checks.result: The current public article explicitly documents trusted gateway identity, hierarchical budgets, estimated-cost reservation before provider dispatch, provider-usage settlement, PostgreSQL, prices, periods, approvals, and orphan handling. It defeats novelty in the reserve-settle gateway integration.

The current documentation explicitly defines remaining budget as total minus reserved minus spent, uses integer microdollars, locks estimated cost before dispatch, and reconciles actual cost afterward. It defeats novelty in the outstanding monetary envelope abstraction.

The ACL record and abstract identify conservative quantile-based request-cost proxies, backlog-aware routing, and admission decisions under uncertain decode length. It defeats novelty in quantile-aware cost admission, although its target is TTFT rather than monetary liability.

The current arXiv record describes estimator-conditional dollar-cap arithmetic, an affine budget mitigation, concurrency-related budget failures, and adaptive rather than static over-reservation. It defeats novelty in generic pre-flight budget reservation and adaptive estimation, while remaining a preprint with an in-process boundary.
The ACL record and abstract explicitly study selecting a model at each turn under a fixed cost budget and analyze model switching. It defeats novelty in generic multi-turn budget state.

The NeurIPS record describes cost-optimal request routing with learned satisfaction probabilities, virtual queues, and SLA constraints. It defeats generic cost-optimal online/SLA and virtual-queue novelty.

The current arXiv record describes online cost-optimal routing from sparse one-sided feedback with SLA guarantees. It defeats sparse-feedback, online adaptation, and SLA-routing novelty, while remaining a preprint and addressing time-average satisfaction rather than a monetary cap.

six_novelty_gate_answers.1_which_exact_element_is_new: None is established as individually new. The only defensible candidate scientific contribution is an evaluated problem and metric formulation that separates request under-reservation, prespecified fixed-cohort exceedance, selected-outstanding-set exceedance, and tenant-window overshoot for priced output-token liabilities under delayed, duplicate, missing, late, and reordered settlement. The corpus supports only an absence-of-found-evidence statement for this exact comparative evaluation, not priority.
six_novelty_gate_answers.2_which_elements_are_known_individually: Cost-quality and budget-constrained routing; joint model and output-budget choice; multi-turn and global budget state; output-length, latency, and cost prediction; conditional quantile admission; conformal and selection-conditioned risk control; sparse or selected-only feedback; online and virtual-queue SLA routing; drift adaptation; dynamic pools; multi-tenant fairness; escrow, idempotence, and transaction recovery; hard policy filtering; pre-dispatch monetary reservation; hierarchical isolation; provider-usage reconciliation; PostgreSQL pending-spend accounting; pricing, periods, approvals, and gateway enforcement are all known individually.
six_novelty_gate_answers.3_what_is_the_closest_prior_work: R55 is the closest implemented reserve-settle gateway, R62 the closest peer-reviewed quantile-aware admission system, R56 the closest documented outstanding monetary envelope, and R01 the closest adaptive reservation and concurrency research preprint. R63/R71, R61/R68, R52/R06/R07, R03/R66, and R45/R46/R49 close the online-SLA, session-budget, calibrated-risk, length-cost, and transaction dimensions respectively.
six_novelty_gate_answers.4_is_the_contribution_more_than_systems_: No. Gateway, PostgreSQL, pending liability, reserve-settle, hierarchy, pricing, approvals, quantile admission, online routing, and budget state all have direct predecessors. The work is scientifically defensible only as an assumption-scoped problem formulation plus preregistered comparative measurement with strong practical and academic comparators, leakage-controlled feedback, explicit fault semantics, and retained null or negative results. The operator is an experimental vehicle, not a novelty claim.
six_novelty_gate_answers.5_what_experiment_would_falsify_the_clai: At matched empirical overshoot risk on identical concurrent delayed-settlement streams, an R55/R56-style atomic fixed-estimate envelope, an R01-style locked adaptive estimator, an R62-style monetary quantile admission policy, or adaptive-quantile reservation plus the cheapest governance-compliant router matches GOV-AR on utilization, served quality, refusal, isolation, and faulty-event outcomes. Advantage language must also be removed if risk allocation does not move the frontier, if full counterfactual leakage is necessary, or if drift and faulty events erase the claimed behavior.
six_novelty_gate_answers.6_which_claim_must_be_removed_or_narrowe: Remove every first-of-kind, universal, integration, and algorithmic claim for cost-aware, budget-constrained, adaptive, conformal, quantile-aware, SLA, sparse-feedback, global-budget, joint model/output-budget, multi-tenant, reserve-settle, budget-envelope, transaction, gateway, governance, or risk-allocation functionality. Do not claim deterministic hard-window safety in nonzero-risk mode. Any probability statement must name its event, cohort, conditioning and selection assumptions, pricing and billing scope, and cannot be generalized to tenant windows or arbitrary selected outstanding sets.

approved_only_if_supported_by_future_fro: An assumption-scoped problem and safety formulation separating settled spend, unresolved estimated-cost liability, request under-reservation, fixed-cohort exceedance, selected-outstanding-set exceedance, and tenant-window overshoot.

A comparative measurement of risk-utilization, tenant isolation, drift, faulty-event behavior, and local overhead against faithful practical envelopes, quantile admission, adaptive estimators, strict reservation, and strong routing baselines.
forbidden: Any first, earliest, unique, unprecedented, universal, or exhaustive priority statement inferred from this corpus
Any independent algorithmic novelty claim for risk allocation, quantile or conformal calibration, online routing, sparse feedback, or joint model and output-budget selection

Any systems-integration novelty claim for reserve-before-dispatch, outstanding budget envelopes, PostgreSQL pending spend, provider-usage reconciliation, hierarchy, approvals, pricing, periods, gateway enforcement, or Kubernetes integration
Any deterministic hard-budget claim for nonzero-risk mode
Any transfer of a fixed-cohort probability bound to tenant-window overshoot or an adaptively selected outstanding set without additional valid assumptions and proof

findings.summary: The stale predecessor review has been replaced by an exact current-corpus-bound review.
Current prior work removes quantile-admission, online-SLA, multi-turn-budget, selected-feedback, envelope, and reserve-settle novelty.
No systems-integration novelty claim survives; only a conditional formulation and comparative measurement boundary is approved.
No algorithmic novelty claim survives, including renamed risk allocation, conformal calibration, or quantile admission.
Independent counts, set equality, and identifier, URL, key, and title deduplication found no retained-corpus inflation.
Search saturation remains explicitly cutoff-scoped and cannot support a first, universal, or exhaustive claim.

progression_verdict: The current literature corpus and novelty boundary satisfy the Article 3 literature red-team condition only. This verdict does not approve implementation, data, protocol freeze, experiments, statistical results, manuscript claims, artifacts, or release. Any corpus-byte change invalidates this approval and requires a fresh source-bound review.
